B1.note: Atari 036174; 32x8 entry PROM. A0-A4 from EAB0-4; D0-D7 share a bus with C1's outputs into the program counter's load inputs (E1 and D1 pins 3-6). Enabled while BEGIN (its CE is /BEGIN), so it supplies the start address of the routine the CPU asked for

B2.section: Control Panel Inputs and Audio Generator
B2.note: POKEY, DIP-40, spans B2 and C2; P0-P7 read the control panel switches directly, D0-D7 on EDB, AUD out through R36/C25

B4.note: JK flip-flop that makes BEGIN: held clear while M START is low, then set on an E6MHZ edge with J = E3MHZ, and toggled off again by its own /BEGIN on K. The second half divides E12KHZ by two to clock the noise shift registers
B4.source: component-location drawing, confirmed by the parts list

C1.note: jump-address latch: takes microcode bits A0-A7 on A6A3 (D5: A16 AND /CLK) and puts them on the program counter's load bus whenever BEGIN is low (OE is BEGIN)
C1.source: component-location drawing, confirmed by the parts list

C3.note: both halves used; one decodes EAB5/EAB6 to SWITCHES, the other EAB3/EAB4 to YHI and YLO
C3.source: component-location drawing, confirmed by the parts list

C4.note: ER/WB and EPHI2 gating into M START
C4.source: component-location drawing, confirmed by the parts list

C5.note: A12 latched by CLK; produces STOP, cleared by BEGIN
C5.source: component-location drawing, confirmed by the parts list

CR2.note: +5V present indicator through R37 (150R). Same designator as the game PCB LED but a different board -- do not confuse the two

D1.note: high half of the microcode program counter; QA-QD (pins 14,13,12,11) drive PROM address A4-A7; QD is also SAEN1 on the signature-analysis header. Loaded with E1 from the same bus
D1.source: component-location drawing, confirmed by the parts list

D2.note: Atari-marked Am2901 4-bit slice, DIP-40; spans D2 and E2, least significant slice -- carry in from microcode bit A23, Q0 shift-in from E3

D3.note: E3MHZ gating; also in the ALU carry path with E5
D3.source: component-location drawing, confirmed by the parts list

D4.note: M START, CLK and STOP gating
D4.source: component-location drawing, confirmed by the parts list

D5.note: A16 and CLK to A6A3, the C1 latch clock
D5.source: component-location drawing, confirmed by the parts list

E1.note: low half of the microcode program counter; QA-QD (pins 14,13,12,11) drive PROM address A0-A3, carry out on 15 into D1. Loads B1's entry address at BEGIN or C1's jump address when the jump condition holds (LD and ET both from D5 pin 11), otherwise counts on CLK
E1.source: component-location drawing, confirmed by the parts list

E3.note: open-collector, EDB7 pulled up by R2 (1k)

E4.note: inverters through the clock and start logic
E4.source: component-location drawing, confirmed by the parts list

E5.note: XOR in the ALU carry path
E5.source: component-location drawing, confirmed by the parts list

F1.note: Atari 036180; microcode PROM, highest microcode field

F2.note: Atari-marked Am2901 4-bit slice, DIP-40; bits 11-8, EDB3-0 under /YHI

F3.section: Control Panel Inputs and Audio Generator
F3.note: engine-rev timer; R10 (100k), R11 (250k pot) and C11 set the rate

F4.section: Control Panel Inputs and Audio Generator
F4.note: motor sound divider, held by MOTOR EN
F4.source: component-location drawing, confirmed by the parts list

F5.section: Control Panel Inputs and Audio Generator
F5.note: second motor sound divider, held by MOTOR EN
F5.source: component-location drawing, confirmed by the parts list

H2.note: Atari-marked Am2901 4-bit slice, DIP-40; spans H2 and J2; bits 7-4, EDB7-4 under /YLO

H4.source: IC parts list, 2 printings, confirmed by the parts list

H5.section: Control Panel Inputs and Audio Generator
H5.note: shift register in the noise generator, fed back through two E5 XOR gates; cleared by SOUND ENABLE
H5.source: component-location drawing, confirmed by the parts list

J3.note: quad analog switch, shell and explosion envelope charge/discharge into C9 and C14

J4.source: component-location drawing, confirmed by the parts list

J5.section: Control Panel Inputs and Audio Generator
J5.source: component-location drawing, confirmed by the parts list

K2.note: Atari-marked Am2901 4-bit slice, DIP-40; most significant slice -- its F3 and OVR feed the sign logic (E5) and its RAM3 is driven by E3 for arithmetic shifts. Puts EDB7-4 on the bus under /YHI

K5.note: quad op-amp on +22V: shell and explosion shapers, engine shaper, and the summing amp that drives AUD+

L4.note: quad analog switch gating shell, explosion and engine paths

M2.note: latches EDB0-7 into MOTOR EN, SOUND ENABLE, ENGINE REV EN, SHELL L/S, SHELL EN, EXPLO L/S and EXPLO EN -- every sound enable on the board comes from this one chip
M2.source: component-location drawing, confirmed by the parts list

M5.note: inverts the mix to give AUD-, so the board puts out a differential pair on edge pins 5 and 6 with AUD RETURN on E
